item.title: Cornell Sexual Assault Investigation to Be Reopened
item.description: After outrage over allegations in a lawsuit, the Tompkins County district attorney will revisit the decision not to pursue criminal charges against seven fraternity members.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman and Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Seth Wenig/Associated Press
item.media:description: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office would reopen the investigation into an alleged 2024 sexual assault following community outrage.

item.title: 30 Ideas for Fixing U.S. Schools, Ranked by Experts
item.description: Math and reading scores are in a decade-long slump. We asked three dozen experts: What could turn things around?
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mervosh, Francesca Paris and Claire Cain Miller
item.media:credit: The New York Times

item.title: Why China Is Requiring Ninth Graders to Read ‘Jane Eyre’
item.description: The Victorian heroine has long been celebrated in China for her independence and insistence on equality.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang and Li You
item.media:credit: Zhu Zhenqiang/VCG, via Getty Images
item.media:description: A woman reads at a bookstore in Beijing in August. “Jane Eyre” has found generations of readers in China since it was first translated into Chinese a century ago.

item.title: At U.C.L.A., a Bollywood Dance Team Like ‘Best of the Best’
item.description: “For a lot of South Asians, dance is the way we connect,” said a member of the U.C.L.A. team Nashaa. Our photographer captured glimpses of the team last year, from audition to competitions.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Bhaskar and Brian Seibert

item.title: Trump Officials Revise How Title IX Sex Discrimination Rules Are Enforced
item.description: The change follows a court ruling barring Title IX from protecting L.G.B.T.Q. people and has angered advocates for sexual assault survivors.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Education Secretary Linda McMahon said the change codifies how the Trump administration has enforced Title IX, the law barring sex discrimination in educational programs funded by the federal government.

item.title: Cambridge Abandons Plans to Fully Investigate Its Hiring of Jason Arday
item.description: The professor had catalyzed debates over diversity efforts in higher education.
item.dc:creator: Mara Hvistendahl
item.media:credit: Chris Radburn/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Tributes to Jason Arday outside Jesus College at the University of Cambridge in England last month.

item.title: 30 College Students Splattered With Condiments and Liquids in Hazing, Police Say
item.description: Two University of Wisconsin-Madison students face charges of suspicion of hazing in the episode, which happened on Wednesday in a sweltering basement, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: An anonymous tip led the police in Madison, Wis., on Wednesday to discover 30 fraternity pledges in a litter-covered basement where the thermostat was set to 81 degrees, officials said.

item.title: Justice Department Scraps Dozens of School Desegregation Cases
item.description: Critics said the changes, mostly in the South, moved the nation “back toward the Jim Crow era.” Justice Department officials said the decrees were outdated.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Gerald Herbert/Associated Press
item.media:description: Vidalia High School, part of Louisiana’s Concordia Parish School District, operated under a court-ordered desegregation plan dating to 1965 until a federal appeals court ended the oversight in July.

item.title: Report Finds Security Failings at Event Where Charlie Kirk Was Killed
item.description: A review commissioned by Utah Valley University faults campus and Turning Point USA officials for poor planning of the event last year.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
item.media:credit: Kim Raff for The New York Times
item.media:description: The site where Charlie Kirk was killed last year at Utah Valley University in Orem, a few days after the shooting.

item.title: American Bar Association Fights to Keep Power to Vet Law Schools
item.description: Losing its accreditation ability would be a blow to the nation’s largest association of lawyers and another example of how the Trump administration is reshaping higher education.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Aaron Schwartz/Sipa USA, Reuters
item.media:description: The Trump administration could strip the American Bar Association of its role in accrediting law schools in the United States.

item.title: Professor Sues New School, Claiming Tenure Has Been Dismantled
item.description: The lawsuit was filed by one of 19 educators laid off in June amid a reorganization of the Manhattan university to address its financial problems.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Tina Fineberg for The New York Times
item.media:description: Hundreds of professors around the world have signed open letters asking for more transparency from the New School about the layoffs.

item.title: Italy Moves to Cap Number of Foreign Students in Its Classrooms
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the goal was to better integrate non-Italian speaking children, but critics accused her of trying to appease anti-immigrant sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Elisabetta Povoledo
item.media:credit: Valentina Stefanelli/LaPresse, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of Italy at a youth festival in Rome last week.

item.title: A Teacher and Activist Admits to Making Up Palestinian Background
item.description: Hannah Gann, who teaches at a Philadelphia high school, said that she had misled people for years and that she is “a white woman of significant privilege.”
item.dc:creator: Jeremy W. Peters

item.title: Ralph Ellison Trust Donates Rights to Bard College
item.description: The liberal arts college announced a center dedicated to the “Invisible Man” author, who taught classes there.
item.dc:creator: Malia Mendez
item.media:credit: Cole Wilson for The New York Times
item.media:description: The center aims to generate scholarship about Ellison and his pursuits across literature and the visual and performing arts.

item.title: Why the Cornell Student Paper Published Names of Accused Men
item.description: Emma Goldberg, a reporter for The Times, tells Natalie Kitroeff, the host of “The Call,” about her coverage of the Cornell student newspaper and its decision to publish the names of seven men accused in a sexual assault case.

item.title: Donor Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon, the Largest University Gift Ever
item.description: The donation by Kenneth Griffin, intended mostly to help build a campus in Miami, was the biggest single gift in the history of U.S. higher education.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Martina Tuaty for The New York Times
item.media:description: The donation from the hedge fund executive Kenneth C. Griffin is more than the record $2 billion gift given to Oregon Health and Science University recently.

item.title: This Case Has Flown Under the Radar. It Won’t Stay There.
item.description: This case has flown under the radar, but it won’t stay there.
item.dc:creator: Linda Greenhouse
item.media:credit: Illustration by Allison DeBritz for The New York Times

item.title: U.S. News Shuffled Its N.Y. High School Rankings. An Uproar Ensued.
item.description: After the New York State Education Department denied a request from U.S. News for A.P. scores, perennially top-ranked schools plummeted.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haag
item.media:credit: Mimi d’Autremont for The New York Times
item.media:description: Robert Kravitz, superintendent of Jericho Union Free School District on Long Island, was upset when his school’s rating plummeted.

item.title: D.A. in Cornell Case Hopes to Speak to Accuser as He Weighs New Evidence
item.description: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said a woman’s report to police in 2024 saying she had been raped at a fraternity did not support a criminal case. But he said he is now reaching out to her.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office
item.media:description: Matthew Van Houten, district attorney for Tompkins County, N.Y., said some new evidence is emerging in an allegation of rape at Cornell University.

item.title: Cornell’s Chi Phi Chapter Faces Scrutiny Over Assault Accusations
item.description: Chi Phi’s Cornell chapter was shuttered after a woman said its members sexually assaulted her. It was one of the oldest fraternities at the school, where Greek life has thrived.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University.

item.title: A Timeline of the Cornell University Rape Investigation
item.description: Prosecutors have reopened an investigation into a former student’s claims that several men sexually assaulted her in a campus fraternity house.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Barnes
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University administrators and the Tompkins County district attorney are under pressure over their handling of a former student’s allegations.

item.title: University of Michigan Halts New Grading Plan After Backlash From Critics
item.description: The program was intended to address what the university called a “mental health crisis.” But the plan was met with criticism that it was coddling students.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin
item.media:credit: Sylvia Jarrus for The New York Times
item.media:description: The University of Michigan campus in Ann Arbor.

item.title: Students at Cornell Daily Sun Pursued Sexual Assault Case for Two Years
item.description: The student newspaper, The Cornell Daily Sun, covered the allegations of rape at a fraternity party since they were first made in 2024 and led the reporting on the case.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Daily Sun is independent of the university and has its offices off campus.
